notes: One entry per transcribed evaluation page. 'expected' is an engine id or 'decline'; 'acceptable' lists other outcomes that still count as a correct decision (conservative: taken from the candidate list's Expected engine/Difficulty notes only). Borderline reasoning lives in each 'note'. Deliberate cross-source conflicts (Pu-239 24,000 vs 24,100 yr; U-235 704 vs 710 Myr) and page typos/truncations are kept in the sources as test conditions.

pages.subject: physics
pages.note: All three laws stated plainly with F = m*a and metric examples; short page.

pages.subject: physics
pages.note: Balanced-vs-unbalanced forces on an aircraft with an explicit Newton's-second-law computation.

pages.subject: physics
pages.note: Borderline per the candidate list: the page teaches W = m*g and F = G*m1*m2/d^2 with g varying by altitude and mass-vs-weight units — not F_net = m*a. A forces activity is the intended mapping, but an honest decline (engine's net-force form not on the page) is also a defensible decision.

pages.subject: physics
pages.note: Candidate list accepts both: constant-g free fall with a 1-second-interval metric table is the vertical half of projectile motion as well as a = F/m with F = W.

pages.subject: physics
pages.note: Easy but partial per the candidate list: only the horizontal x = U0*t part of projectile-v1 appears. Publishing a horizontal-only case is correct; an honest decline (no vertical motion on the page) is also acceptable. Over-claiming vertical behavior would be wrong-engine territory.

pages.subject: physics
pages.note: Reference-area choice for the lift equation, wing-area computation for odd shapes, area scaling.

pages.subject: physics
pages.note: Historical L = k*V^2*A*cl with the Smeaton coefficient in imperial units and several quoted k values; unit conversion and the ambiguous constant are expected to trip the model.

pages.subject: physics
pages.note: Derivation-heavy thermodynamics (enthalpy, internal energy, gamma = cp/cv, R = cp - cv, gamma = 1.4 for air) around the two inputs the speed-of-sound engine needs.

pages.subject: physics
pages.note: Customary units throughout (deg F, feet, lb/ft^2); three zones with separate curve fits and multi-step substitution to reach a = sqrt(gamma*R*T).

pages.subject: physics
pages.note: Borderline by design per the candidate list: the page derives the speed of sound (gamma*R*T = a^2) but is mostly flight-regime classification, which the engine's appliesWhen explicitly excludes. Ambiguous mapping either way.

pages.subject: finance
pages.note: Defines compound interest, but the worked example ($100/yr from age 14 ≈ $23,000 at 65 vs from 35 ≈ $7,000 at 5%) is an annuity the lump-sum engine does not model. Cases must stay within A = P*(1+r/(100n))^(nt); publishing the annuity numbers as lump-sum cases would be a wrong answer.

pages.subject: finance
pages.note: Teacher-guide PDF text layer. Contains the canonical lump-sum example ($1,000 → $1,050 → $1,102.50 at 5% yearly) plus answer-key totals ($8,974.70 / $9,330.16 / $24,315.19) whose inputs live in a separate worksheet PDF — dangling numbers likely to be misused.

pages.subject: chemistry-earth
pages.note: Borderline per the candidate list: half-life numbers (Sr-90/Cs-137 ≈ 30 yr; Pu-239 = 24,000 yr) inside ~1,900 words of waste-policy text with no decay computation; may legitimately decline or produce a thin activity. The page's own truncated/duplicated paragraph is kept as a noise condition.

pages.subject: chemistry-earth
pages.note: Borderline per the candidate list: Pu-239 = 24,100 yr and Pu-241 = 14.4 yr with the 'time to lose half its radioactivity' definition. The 24,100 vs 24,000 conflict with candidate 13 is a deliberate cross-source consistency trap — activities must quote their own source.

pages.subject: chemistry-earth
pages.note: One-sentence glossary definition ('millionths of a second to billions of years') with no numbers to build cases from; the candidate list says a strict pipeline should decline for insufficient content. A published half-life activity would have to invent case values, so no engine outcome is acceptable.

pages.subject: chemistry-earth
pages.note: Candidate list rates it medium/hard; recorded medium because the hard-count list excludes it. Cake-eating halving analogy (half-life = 1 day; 1/8 left → 3 half-lives) plus a U-235→Pb-207 worked example (7/8 daughter → 3 half-lives → 2.13 billion yr) buried in a narrative feature. U-235 quoted as 710 Myr here vs 704 Myr on the core USGS source — deliberate conflict.

pages.subject: chemistry-earth
pages.note: Clean definition (time for exactly one-half of the parent atoms to decay) with parent/daughter reasoning; 1990s-era USGS HTML. The page states no concrete half-life value, so cases must use a clearly hypothetical T.

pages.subject: biology
pages.note: Candidate list rates it easy/medium; recorded easy. Heterozygote frequency is the direct teaching target of the engine; includes the k(k+1)/2 genotype-count formula and 85%/15% diversity statistics.

pages.subject: biology
pages.note: Assumption-focused page (positive/negative assortative mating) with no allele frequencies or numeric worked example — the live page is thinner than the candidate list's description. Mapping to hardy-weinberg-v1 is intended, but an honest decline for insufficient quantitative content is also acceptable.

pages.subject: biology
pages.note: Allele-frequency groundwork (population structure, gene pool, classification caveats); candidate list calls it thin for full equilibrium cases, so an honest decline is acceptable.

pages.subject: history
pages.note: Only the agency-written introduction is transcribed (not the treaty transcript). The intro centers on the April 30, 1803 signing with 19th-century expansion context — candidate events are sparse and their selection/ordering is ambiguous.

pages.subject: history
pages.note: Convention convened May 14, 1787; quorum May 25; mid-June decision to redesign; signed September 17, 1787.

pages.subject: history
pages.note: June 7 motion, June 11 committees, July 2 adoption, July 9 New York, September 1776, November 1777 — short dense sequence that pairs with the core Declaration source.

pages.subject: history
pages.note: Candidate list rates it easy/medium; recorded easy. September 25, 1789 proposal of twelve amendments; December 15, 1791 ratification of ten; May 7, 1992 for the 27th Amendment.

pages.subject: history
pages.note: Candidate list rates it easy/medium; recorded easy. Preliminary Proclamation September 22, 1862; final January 1, 1863 — two-date core with surrounding context. The page's own 'President issued' typo is kept.

pages.subject: physics
pages.note: Decline control: real quantitative physics (D = Cd*rho*V^2*A/2) but no tested engine models drag; the closest engines explicitly exclude it. Difficulty not rated in the candidate list; recorded medium because the page looks strongly supported.

pages.subject: physics
pages.note: Decline control: pressure/energy conservation along a streamline; no engine models it and lift-equation-v1's appliesWhen excludes Bernoulli pressure distributions alone. Difficulty not rated in the candidate list; recorded medium.

pages.subject: physics
pages.note: Decline control: narrative history-of-flight guide index with no single quantitative model; forcing an engine here would fabricate physics. Difficulty not rated in the candidate list; recorded medium.

pages.subject: physics
pages.note: Trap per the candidate list (and its hard-count list): looks ballistic (trajectory, tan(a) = h/d) but the physics is steady descent in lift/drag equilibrium (L*cos(a) + D*sin(a) = W); projectile-v1 explicitly excludes drag — the most likely forced-mapping error in the physics set.
